cards.question: The shofar heard at Jewish New Year is traditionally fashioned from what?
cards.answerExplanation: The shofar is an actual animal horn, used as a wind instrument. Its blasts at Rosh Hashanah call listeners to reflection and repentance.
cards.whyNow: A September 11 presidential message marks Rosh Hashanah, bringing the holiday and its distinctive shofar tradition into focus.

cards.question: A bottle of 12-year-old Scotch stays unopened for 20 more years. How much is added to the whisky’s stated age?
cards.answerExplanation: Whisky matures in the cask, not the bottle. A longer stay on a shelf makes the bottle older without adding years to the whisky's age statement.
cards.whyNow: English Whisky received protected geographical status on September 11, putting how whisky is made and described back in the news.

newsPegSources.headline: English Whisky raises a glass to new protected status

cards.question: The dark-line pattern in a star's spectrum acts like a fingerprint of what?
cards.answerExplanation: Gases absorb particular colours of starlight, leaving dark lines. Each element has its own pattern, so astronomers can identify stellar ingredients without travelling to the star.
cards.whyNow: NASA’s September 11 introduction of Artifact InSPECtor highlights telescope spectra, the rainbow patterns that reveal what distant objects contain.

coreFactSources.title: Imagine the Universe: Spectral Analysis Appendix

newsPegSources.headline: Help Refine Data from Space Telescopes with Artifact InSPECtor

cards.question: Why do astronauts and loose objects float together inside an orbiting space station?
choices: The station shields them from gravity
Earth's gravity ends at that height
They and the station fall together
cards.canonicalAnswer: They and the station fall together
cards.answerExplanation: The station, crew and loose objects are in continuous free fall around Earth. They fall together, while moving sideways fast enough to keep missing the ground; gravity has not switched off.
cards.whyNow: NASA announced a September 16 Crew-12 news conference from the space station ahead of the crew’s return, bringing daily life in orbit into focus.

newsPegSources.headline: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 to Discuss Station Mission, Upcoming Return

cards.question: A tree can still draw water after losing a ring of bark. What supply is chiefly cut off?
choices: Minerals moving up from the roots
Sugars moving out of the leaves
Water moving up inside the trunk
cards.canonicalAnswer: Sugars moving out of the leaves
cards.answerExplanation: Ring-barking severs phloem, the route carrying sugars out of leaves. Water can still move through the intact xylem, but that does not replace the interrupted food supply.
cards.whyNow: A September 12 feature on rewilding art describes ring-barking trees to create deadwood habitat, a striking example of how bark keeps a tree alive.

coreFactSources.title: Carbohydrate regulation of photosynthesis and respiration from branch girdling in four species of wet tropical rain forest trees
